question.leadin: Answer these questions about American business tycoons.
question.text: Nicknamed "Commodore", this builder of the New York Central Railroad founded a university named after him in Nashville, Tennessee.
question.clue: During the California Gold Rush, this person created the Accessory Transit Company to bring passengers from the East Coast to San Francisco via Nicaragua.

swap.leadin: This woman was convicted in 1872 for illegally voting, but refused to pay the fine.
swap.text: Name this champion of women's suffrage who was featured on the 1979 one dollar coin.
swap.clue: This woman is the alleged author of "Marriage and Maternity," an article published in The Revolution.

question.leadin: In 1973, members of the American Indian Movement led an armed occupation of this town as a protest against federal treatment of Native Americans.
question.text: Name this small town where, 83 years earlier, Spotted Elk and over one hundred Lakota people were massacred by the 7th Cavalry.
question.clue: The Big Foot Memorial Riders end their path at this place, remembering an event that began due to Black Coyote's deafness.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about presidential assassinations.
swap.text: This immigrant, a disciple of the anarchist Emma Goldman, traveled to Buffalo and shot William McKinley in a reception line at the 1901 Pan-American Exposition.
swap.clue: Note to Moderator: Be generous on pronunciation. While Robert Todd Lincoln was outside the Temple of Music at the 1901 Pan-American Exposition in Buffalo, New York, this anarchist shot William McKinley.

question.text: This Carnegie steel manager was primarily responsible for handling the Pinkertons. Almost assassinated by Alexander Berkman, this man also owned a whiskey company with Andrew Mellon.
question.clue: Joseph Duveen advised this man on purchasing works like Vermeer's Officer and Laughing Girl for his Fifth Avenue mansion.

swap.leadin: This event began with newspaper editor August Spies (speez) and Reverend Samuel Fielden addressing a crowd in front of McCormick Harvesting Machine Company.
swap.text: Name this 1886 disturbance, during which a pipe bomb killed Mathias Degan (DEE-guhn). This event damaged the reputation of the Knights of Labor and inspired the May Day holiday.
swap.clue: The day prior to this event, August Spies told a group of striking workers to "hold together... stand by their union" during a speech at the McCormick Harvesting Machine Co. plant.

question.text: The Ghost Dance movement started to decline after this massacre in which the U.S. military killed several hundred Lakota people on the Pine Ridge reservation.
question.clue: This event began at Pine Ridge after one side engaged the Miniconjou and Chief Big Foot surrendered.

swap.text: Guiteau assassinated this president, who served only seven months in office. This man's Secretary of State was James Blaine, and he was succeeded by Chester A. Arthur.
swap.clue: This man defeated Winfield Scott Hancock to become president, and the Pendleton Civil Service Act was passed after his death.

question.leadin: This movement had two phases, both started by Nevada Paiute.
question.text: Wodziwob and Wovoka were the leaders of what religious revival among Plains Indians, which promised an end to white supremacy if certain movements were performed?
question.clue: "Garments" in the Book of Mormon may have inspired the belief that clothes worn by this movement's adherents would gain resistance to bullets.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about some influential political cartoons in American history.
swap.text: An early color cartoon from Puck magazine lampooned this presidential candidate as the "tattooed man" whose body was covered in a sea of scandals. His namesake amendments barred government funding for parochial schools.
swap.clue: Samuel Burchard hurt this man's presidential bid after claiming that the other party represented "Rum, Romanism, and Rebellion".

question.leadin: As Governor, this man helped to take down the corrupt "Canal Ring."
question.text: Name this man who earned his reputation battling Boss Tweed and Tammany Hall. He lost his most notable election thanks to a political compromise promising to remove federal troops from former Confederate states.
question.clue: This man denied having sent the Cipher Dispatches and bequeathed four million dollars to a trust that helped establish the original New York City Public Library.

swap.leadin: Rural Free Delivery, or the right for people in remote agricultural areas to receive mail for free, was one political goal of this group, whose midsized conglomerates were named for Pomona, the Roman goddess of agricultural abundance.
swap.text: Name this organization, established after Andrew Johnson commissioned Oliver Kelley to take a tour of the southern states. Founded in 1867, it remains the oldest active American agricultural advocacy group.
swap.answerHtml: The Grange [accept The National Grange of the Order of Patrons of Husbandry; accept Grangers]
swap.clue: This organization was formed in 1867 by Oliver Kelley to ensure the rights of farmers. It won a major victory on private warehouses in the court case Munn v. Illinois.

question.text: John F. Stevens surveyed Montana for this railway led by James J. Hill, whose route crossed Marias Pass and Glacier National Park. Amtrak now operates this former competitor of Northern Pacific with a mountain goat logo.
question.answerHtml: Great Northern Railway [or GN; accept Empire Builder; accept Burlington Northern and Santa Fe or or BNSF]

swap.text: This Missouri Congressman lost the 1896 Democratic nomination to Bryan after the speech and was chairman of the Committee on Coinage, Weights, and Measures.
swap.clue: American History (Allison) Iowa Senator William Allison revised this Representative's original bill, calling for a monthly limit of $2-4 million worth in silver for coinage purposes.

question.leadin: Henry Littlefield wrote a 1964 article claiming that this book is a metaphor for monetary policy debates.
question.text: Name this 1900 children's book whose prominent featuring of the metals gold and silver lends some cre-dence that its author may have been thinking of Populist debates when he wrote it.
question.answerHtml: The Wizard of Oz [or The Wonderful Wizard of Oz]
question.clue: Quentin Taylor's reading of this book asserts that a trio of characters in it represent respectively, farmers, the steel industry, and the American performance in the Spanish-American War.

swap.leadin: The Hayden Expedition to this location issued propaganda that its natives were afraid of geysers to increase tourism.
swap.text: Name this first U.S. national park that was established in 1872.
swap.clue: One early success of the conservationist movement was the designation of this first national park, located primarily in Wyoming. The Old Faithful geyser can be found in this park.

question.leadin: Name these great contributors to the history of Montana.
question.text: This Canadian-American magnate expanded the St. Paul and Pacific Railroad into the transcontinental Great Northern Railway, earning him the epithet "Empire Builder," and bringing trade to the entire Northwestern US, including Montana.

swap.text: Blaine's election strategy relied on Irish-American voters' defections on account of Blaine's ancestry, but this man's speech decrying "Rum, Romanism, and Rebellion" torpedoed that plan.

question.leadin: A chapter of this book titled "The Dynamo and the Virgin" details the protagonist's visit to the Great Exhibition of 1900 with the scientist Samuel Langley.
question.text: Name this book that documents the protagonist's perspective on growing up during the changes of the Second Industrial Revolution. It was intended as a modern sequel to its author's Mont-Saint-Michel and Chartres.
question.clue: It describes difficulties in finding a publisher for an article exposing Jay Gould and laments learning Latin and Greek instead of French and German.

swap.leadin: A 2015 biography by Edward O'Donnell titled [this man] and the Crisis of Inequality casts him as a social reformer whose ideas foreshadowed the Progressive Era and the New Deal.
swap.text: Name this United Labor Party candidate who finished second in the hotly contested 1886 mayoral race in New York City, where he faced off against Tammany Hall's Abram Hewitt and Republican upstart Theodore Roosevelt.
swap.clue: This man advocated a single tax on land as a solution for breaking the cycle of poverty in Progress and Poverty.
